subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finpay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of requirements (from the call):
- Core use case: real-time fraud scoring on payment flows (decisioning path must be highly predictable)
- Typical steady-state traffic: ~200 QPS (requests/sec)
- Peak/spike traffic: up to ~800 QPS during US business hours (5–10min bursts expected)
- Latency target: P95 < 100ms for inference; ideal target P95 < 75ms for critical flows
- Payload: short prompts (~120 tokens) with light post-processing
- Data considerations: PII stripped upstream; FinPay prefers data isolation for production

What we discussed as options:
- Hosted API: fast to get started, auto-scaling, lower upfront friction — may have more variable latency at high sustained QPS unless we move to reserved capacity
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and latency, SLA-backed targets, recommended for sustained high QPS and strict p95s
- Private/VPC: available for full isolation (usually later in procurement, not required for initial rollout)

Attachments: I’ve attached our internal dedicated benchmarks (redwood-dedicated-qps-latency.pdf) and a simple capacity worksheet (capacity-sizing.xlsx) to help model costs.

Proposed next steps:
1) FinPay: confirm the steady-state and spike QPS numbers above and provide an internal procurement timeline (Eve or procurement contact).
2) Redwood: we’ll size a recommended Dedicated pool (GPU types, slot counts) and provide indicative pricing + SLA options.
3) Technical validation: offer a 2-week Hosted POC to validate end-to-end latency and integration, then flip to Dedicated for production if you need the guaranteed throughput/latency.
4) If you want to move directly to Dedicated, we can draft an SOW and get procurement engaged.

Would you like us to size Dedicated now or run the quick Hosted POC first? I’m available this week for a capacity sizing call with your infra/procurement folks.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Alex Porter <alex.porter@finpay.com>

Cc: Eve Tran <eve.tran@finpay.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Thanks Neha — helpful recap. Couple of clarifications from our side:

- Confirm steady-state: 180–220 QPS (avg 200)
- Spikes: we’ve seen up to ~900 QPS in Black Friday-like runs, but typical short bursts are 600–800 QPS (~5–8 minutes)
- Latency requirement: P95 <= 75ms for fraud decision flow is preferred; we can tolerate up to 120ms for lower-priority scoring jobs
- Data isolation: for production this is desirable — we need a compliance check but can start POC without private VPC
- SLOs: procurement will ask about SLA credits and uptime targets for Dedicated

Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to finalize a vendor and procurement terms in ~6 weeks (target: mid-August). Internal procurement lead is Eve (cc’d).

Next actions from FinPay:
- Eve will share procurement checklist and timeline.
- We’d like an indicative Dedicated monthly cost and also Hosted POC terms (duration, rate cap) so procurement can evaluate both.

If it helps, we’re open to a short Hosted POC for 2 weeks to validate integration and latency under realistic traffic; if numbers are in line we’ll move to Dedicated for production.

Appreciate the quick sizing — can Dylan help with expected GPU type/slot count for a Dedicated pool sized for sustained 200 QPS with headroom for 800 QPS spikes?

Cheers,
Alex Porter
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPay
alex.porter@finpay.com

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 12:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up

Alex / Eve — thanks, that matches what I heard. Quick recommendation and proposed timeline: 

Recommendation:
- For FinPay’s requirements (steady ~200 QPS with frequent 600–900 QPS spikes and P95 target <= 75ms for critical flows), Dedicated capacity is the recommended production configuration. Dedicated GPU pools give predictable per-token performance, reserved throughput, and the SLA protections procurement will want.

POC path (recommended):
1) Run a 2-week Hosted POC (we’ll provide a capped trial rate) to validate integration latency and edge cases — this reduces time-to-value and lets your engineers validate instrumentation and prometheus traces.
2) Parallel capacity sizing: Dylan to propose a Dedicated pool config (GPU type, number of slots) in a separate note — that will include cost estimates and warm-up/eviction behaviors during spikes.
3) If POC passes, move to Dedicated: we’ll draft a short SOW (SOW-draft.pdf) and start procurement discussions. We can target production cutover in ~4–6 weeks after procurement sign-off.

Dylan — can you take the sizing/numbers action? Something like: recommended baseline for 200 steady QPS + 4x headroom for spikes (target 800–900) plus notes on autoscale buffer and warm cache sizing. If you prefer, I can set a 30-min call with Alex and Eve today or tomorrow.

Eve — I’ll include the Dedicated pricing bands and SLA options in the SOW draft. Also happy to provide SOC2 evidence and a short compliance packet during procurement.

Next steps (owners & timing):
- FinPay: confirm procurement timeline (Eve) — due by EOD Thursday if possible.
- Redwood (Dylan): capacity sizing note + rough monthly pricing (by end of day tomorrow).
- Redwood (Neha): Hosted POC terms and trial cap (sent in separate email).

Thanks — we’ll follow up with the capacity worksheet filled and SOW draft.

Best,
